title: Software Testing Examples
description: Small Software Testing examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Expected and actual results
examples.description: A test compares an expected result with the actual result. A passing test only checks the case you gave it.
examples.code:
const add = (a, b) => a + b;
console.log(add(2, 3) === 5);

examples.title: Choose useful cases
examples.description: A test case includes inputs and the expected result. Choose cases that exercise different rules.
examples.code:
const isFree = age => age < 5;
console.log(isFree(3), isFree(8));

examples.title: Boundaries catch small mistakes
examples.description: A boundary is where a rule changes. Values just before, on and after it are especially useful tests.
examples.code:
const canEnter = age => age >= 10;
console.log(canEnter(9), canEnter(10), canEnter(11));

examples.title: Empty input is a real case
examples.description: An empty list has no items. Decide what your program should do with it before writing a test.
examples.code:
const total = values => values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0);
console.log(total([]));

examples.title: Negative tests
examples.description: A negative test checks how a program rejects an invalid input. The expected result may be a useful error instead of a normal value.

examples.title: Unit and integration tests
examples.description: A unit test checks a small part. An integration test checks parts working together. Each finds different mistakes.
examples.code:
Unit: price(2, 3) returns 6
Integration: basket passes its items to the price calculator
End-to-end: a learner adds an item and sees the total

examples.title: Make a bug report useful
examples.description: A bug report should let another person repeat the problem. Include steps, expected behaviour and actual behaviour.
examples.code:
Steps: open quiz, answer 2 questions, press Next
Expected: question 3 appears
Actual: question 2 stays visible
Browser: the browser used for the test

examples.title: Regression tests protect fixes
examples.description: A regression happens when something that worked stops working. Add a test for a fixed bug so later changes check it again.
examples.code:
Bug: empty basket crashed
Fix: use zero as the starting total
Regression test: empty basket total equals zero

examples.title: Repeatable tests
examples.description: A repeatable test gives the same result with the same inputs. Pass changing values in instead of hiding the current time in the calculation.
examples.code:
const isLate = (due, today) => today > due;
console.log(isLate(5, 6));

examples.title: Explore with a question
examples.description: Exploratory testing uses a goal and careful observation. You choose the next step from what you discover.
examples.code:
Goal: can I use the search with only a keyboard?
Try: Tab to search, type a word, press Enter
Record: focus order, result, unexpected behaviour

examples.title: Accessibility is part of quality
examples.description: Accessibility means people with different needs can use the app. Test labels, keyboard access and visible focus as well as mouse clicks.
examples.code:
Input label: Search lessons
Keyboard: Tab reaches input; Enter submits
Focus: a visible border marks the active control

examples.title: Report what was checked
examples.description: A test summary says what ran, what passed and what remains unchecked. It should not promise more than the evidence supports.
examples.code:
Checked: search, lesson links, quiz scoring
Passed: 14 cases
Failed: 1 keyboard case
Not checked: old browser versions
